# Brno specialities for level design

Researched 2026-10-17 with live web access (curl against Wikipedia's API, official sites, DuckDuckGo).
Every fact below comes from the source linked next to it. Anything I could not confirm is marked
**UNVERIFIED** or listed under "Not confirmed". cs.wikipedia links use the article title. Short form:
`csw:<Title>` = `https://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/<Title>`.

## 1. Legends

| Legend | Confirmed facts | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **Brno dragon** (Brněnský drak) | A stuffed **crocodile** hangs from the ceiling of the Old Town Hall passage. The most common story says Archduke/Margrave Matthias gave it in 1608. Town accounts show it was already being restored and treated for worms in 1578–79. It is first recorded in 1568, when a painter painted it for 4 guilders. Folk version: brave townsmen fed the dragon a leather bag of **quicklime**; it got thirsty, drank, and burst. | csw:Brněnský_drak, csw:Stará_radnice_(Brno) |
| **Brno wheel** (Brněnské kolo) | Wheelwright **Georg (Jiří) Birck from Lednice** bet 12 thalers in a pub. He said that between sunrise and sunset he would fell a tree, make a wheel from it and roll it **~54 km to Brno**. He won, so the wheel hangs in the Town Hall passage. Date: 14 May **1635** (wheel article) or **1636** (Town Hall article), so the sources disagree. People said the devil helped him. Real wheel: 144 cm across, 12 spokes. A survey showed it was made in a workshop from more than one wood. A yearly re-enactment proves the roll can be done in a day. | csw:Brněnské_kolo, csw:Stará_radnice_(Brno) |
| **Crooked pinnacle** (pokroucená fiála) | Anton Pilgram built the Old Town Hall portal in **1510–1511**. Of its five pinnacles, the **middle one is bent**. Legend: the councillors did not pay him in full, so he bent it on purpose, "crooked like justice in Brno". He then left for Vienna to work on St. Stephen's Cathedral. | csw:Stará_radnice_(Brno) |
| **Rude little man** (neslušný mužíček), St. James | In a window arch of the St. James tower that faces náměstí Svobody, a figure **shows its bare bottom toward Petrov** (the cathedral of Sts Peter and Paul). The story: St. James (92 m) beat Petrov (84 m) in a "which tower is taller" contest. That version can only date from the early 1900s, because the Petrov towers were built in 1908. Another version: the Petrov chapter drove the builder out, and his last wish was to finish this window. Actually it is **two figures embracing**, a man and a "rude little woman". The heads were added in 1937. | csw:Kostel_svatého_Jakuba_(Brno) |
| **Noon at 11:00** (Petrov) | Swedes under Torstenson besieged Brno in 1645. Legend: Torstenson swore to leave if the city had not fallen by noon on 15 August, so the defenders rang noon an hour early, and the Petrov bells still ring noon at 11:00. In reality the general assault lasted until evening and was fully beaten back. The defence was led by Louis Raduit de Souches. A priest, Martin Středa, rallied people with "Kdo brání Brno, brání celou Moravu" (whoever defends Brno defends all of Moravia). | csw:Obléhání_Brna_(1645) |
| **Astronomical clock** (Brněnský orloj), nám. Svobody | Black stone ("black granite" = gabbro from South Africa), **about 6 m tall**, **shaped like a bullet**. Unveiled 18 Sep 2010 and cost CZK 12 million. Every day at **11:00** a **glass marble** rolls out into one of **4 holes**, and whoever catches it keeps it. Marbles from the Karlov glassworks. Chimes play at 10:15, 10:30, 10:45 and 11:00. Reading the time from it is notoriously hard. The public calls it "falické hodiny" or "Brněnský falus" (phallic clock) and compares it to a giant vibrator. Nobody caught the first marble at the unveiling. It is wrapped in a fireproof inflatable cover every New Year's Eve. | csw:Brněnský_orloj |
| **Mendel's peas** | Abbot of the Augustinian abbey in Staré Brno. From **1856 to 1863** he crossed **peas**, and the result became Mendel's laws. He also kept **bees**: he built a bee house in 1871. And he made daily weather observations (9 of his 13 papers are on meteorology). The foundations of his 1854 greenhouse survive. | csw:Gregor_Johann_Mendel, csw:Mendelovo_muzeum |
| **Capuchin crypt** | Burials took place here from 1656 to 1784. Clever ventilation openings **mummified bodies naturally**. About 200 people are buried there, about 150 of them friars. It also holds baron **Franz von Trenck** (d. 1749), commander of the pandurs, in a tin coffin. | csw:Kapucínská_hrobka_(Brno) |
| **St. James ossuary** | It holds the remains of up to **50,000 people** and is the **2nd largest ossuary in Europe after Paris**. It was rediscovered in 2001 and opened to the public in 2012. Before that, the only way in was a hatch in the pavement and a ladder. | csw:Kostnice_u_svatého_Jakuba |
| **Labyrinth under Zelný trh** | Historic cellars under the cabbage market, opened to the public in 2011 and run by TIC Brno. | csw:Labyrint_pod_Zelným_trhem |
| **Ponávka** | This stream used to flow right through Brno. It was piped underground in the late 1800s and part of its bed became the main sewer. Since 1993 it has been diverted into a 3 km tunnel. A 320 m artificial stream in Lužánky (2005) roughly follows its old course. | csw:Ponávka |
| **Macocha** (near Brno) | The abyss is **138.4 m** deep. Legend: a stepmother (*macecha*) pushed her stepson in. He caught on a ledge and was rescued, and the villagers then threw her in. The story was first recorded in 1793. | csw:Propast_Macocha |

## 2. Hantec

Hantec mixes Moravian dialect with Brno German, Viennese argot, Yiddish and Romani. In **August 2026** it
was added to the South Moravian Region's list of intangible folk culture (csw:Hantec;
https://www.blesk.cz/clanek/regiony-brno-brnane/842554/salina-prygl-hokna-hantec-je-v-seznamu-pokladu-lidove-kultury.html).
Word sources: csw:Hantec, the en.wikipedia "Hantec slang" table (citing *Velký slovník hantecu*), and
http://www.hantec.cz/hantec/slovnik/slovnik.htm (the HC column below).

| Word | Meaning | Src |
|---|---|---|
| šalina | tram (German *elektrische Linie*); the transit company sells the "šalinkarta" pass | csw, HC |
| štatl / Štatl | town or city centre, Brno; *štatlit* = to go | en, HC |
| betálný | excellent, beautiful (*Betálný Štatl* = beautiful Brno) | en, HC |
| zoncna | sun; *zoncna rumpluje / vaří* = the sun is scorching | csw, HC |
| hokna / hoknit | work / to work | csw, HC |
| čurina | fun, a laugh | csw, HC |
| škopek | beer (also head); *kalit škopky* = drink beers | csw, HC |
| love | money (from Romani) | csw, HC |
| Prýgl / Prigl | Brno Reservoir | csw:Brněnská_přehrada, HC |
| koc / kocór | girl | csw, HC |
| čórka | theft | csw, HC |
| šaškec | madhouse, mess | csw, HC |
| rola | main railway station | csw, HC |
| retych | toilet | en |
| augle | eyes | en, HC |
| gómat | understand, know | en, HC |
| lochec | laughter | en, HC |
| švimhózny | swimsuit (*jak švimhózny na priglu* = useless) | en |
| šlofnót / šlofík | sleep / nap | en, HC |
| ksicht | face | HC |
| plotna | a gang or group of people | HC |
| cajzl | someone from Bohemia / Prague (**can offend**) | csw, HC |
| rožnout | switch on the light | csw |

**Place nicknames, confirmed:** Špilas (Špilberk; also Špéna), Prýgl, Monte Bú and **Kravák** (Kraví
hora), Augec (Lužánky), Oltec (Staré Brno), Šrajbec (Pisárky), Bástr (Bystrc), Žabiny (Žabovřesky),
Kénik / Krpole (Královo Pole), Šimice (Židenice), Blekfíld (Černá Pole), Majlont (Maloměřice), Čára
(Česká street), Osmec or Wintrák (nám. 28. října), **Svoboďák** (nám. Svobody,
csw:Náměstí_Svobody_(Brno)), **Jakubák** (Jakubské nám.; the bars there formed a "spolek Jakubák",
https://vycepnastojaka.cz/vycepy/jakubak-brno/), **Palačák** (the VUT campus Pod Palackého vrchem),
Fléda (the club). In 2018 a public poll to name the new main station was won by "**Brno–Šalingrad**".

**Not confirmed, so do not use:** *rína*, *hecnout*, *Bany*, *Mendlák*. I found no reliable source for
these.

## 3. Places: visuals + mechanic hook

- **Zelný trh + Parnas**: a baroque fountain (1690–96, by Fischer von Erlach) built as a rocky cliff. In its
  cave stands Hercules holding the **three-headed Cerberus** on a chain, and Europa stands on top over a slain
  dragon. Three seated women represent Greece, Babylon and Persia, with a winged dragon, a lion and a **bear
  climbing out of the rock**. "Parnas" is a mistake: Jesuit students took the statues for Muses. The fountain
  has been vandalised since at least 1808 (csw:Parnas_(kašna)). The Reduta theatre on the same square is
  where **11-year-old Mozart** played with his sister Nannerl in December 1767 (csw:Divadlo_Reduta).
- **Old Town Hall**: the tower is 62.66 m tall with **173 steps**. The dragon, the wheel and the bent
  pinnacle are all at its gate (csw:Stará_radnice_(Brno)).
- **Vila Tugendhat** (Mies van der Rohe, 1929–30, UNESCO since 2001): the **onyx wall** changes colour as
  the setting sun shines through it. **Two huge glass panes (5 × 3.5 m) slide down into the floor.** One
  pane survived a 1945 bomb blast because it was lowered at the time. The Red Army stabled **horses** in
  the house. The Czechoslovak split was negotiated there in 1992 (csw:Vila_Tugendhat).
- **Špilberk**: a 13th-century castle turned baroque fortress whose **casemates** became a feared prison
  in 1783. Prisoners included Trenck and the Italian poet Silvio Pellico (csw:Špilberk).
- **Hvězdárna (observatory), Kraví hora**: opened 1954. The top of its dome (318 m above sea level) is the
  highest point for kilometres around (csw:Hvězdárna_a_planetárium_Brno).
- **Výstaviště** (exhibition grounds): built in **14 months**, opened 1928. Functionalist pavilions and
  domed halls (csw:Výstaviště_Brno).
- **Masarykův okruh**: built 1985–87 in the woods. MotoGP Czech GP until 2020, **brought back in 2025**
  (csw:Masarykův_okruh).
- **Ignis Brunensis**: firework competition since 1998. Shows are fired **from the reservoir's water
  surface**, plus Petrov and Špilberk (csw:Ignis_Brunensis).
- **AZ Tower**: **111 m**, the tallest building in Czechia (2013) (csw:AZ_Tower).
- **Brno Reservoir (Prýgl)**: a flooded valley that drowned the village of Kníničky
  (csw:Brněnská_přehrada). **ZOO** is nearby on Mniší hora: about 2,200 animals, and it bred a
  **polar bear** (csw:Zoologická_zahrada_Brno).
- **Starobrno brewery**: has brewed since **1325**. A beer named after the dragon exists
  (csw:Pivovar_Starobrno, csw:Brněnský_drak).
- Not verified in detail (skipped for space): Kometa fan culture, Janáček Theatre (opened 1965), and the
  Kounicovy koleje dorm history (see section 4).

## 4. Student spots

- **Jakubák**: the St. James square and its bars. **Výčep Na stojáka** ("the standing pub") opened
  **5 April 2013**. Its owners say the square then became one of the busiest spots in the centre. In 2017
  the bars formed the "spolek Jakubák" (https://vycepnastojaka.cz/vycepy/jakubak-brno/). Hook: the
  rude bum-man and the ossuary are **right underneath**, and the Zlatá studna well (10 m deep, rebuilt
  2007, with a snake and a bird spouting water) is on the same square (csw:Jakubské_náměstí_(Brno)).
- **Bar, který neexistuje** ("the bar that does not exist"), Dvořákova 1: the name follows the
  speakeasy tradition, and the **entrance is deliberately easy to miss**. The wall is shelved with bottles
  up to the ceiling (https://www.brnolove.cz/bar-ktery-neexistuje-recenze/,
  https://www.lidizbaru.cz/cs/bar-ktery-neexistuje).
- **Fléda**: a club since 2001 in the building of the 1911 cabaret **Brünner Fledermaus** ("Brno
  bat"), which is where the name comes from. It also hosts open-airs on Špilberk (csw:Fléda).
- **Noční rozjezd** (night dispersal): **every night bus meets at the main station every 60 (or 30)
  minutes** so passengers can change, then they all leave at once. In 2016 it carried about 10k riders on
  ordinary nights and **25–26k on Wednesdays and Fridays, mostly students** (Brno has 70k+). The busiest
  time is 23:00–0:30. A 2011 comic "Brněnské rozjezdy" got 200k views (csw:Městská_autobusová_doprava_v_Brně,
  csw:Rozjezd).
- **Pod Palackého vrchem ("Palačák")**: VUT campus with 4 faculties, dorms and **5 canteens**. Engineering
  graduates paint "**Ing. nickname**" signatures on pavements and roads. On a roughly 100 m wall in Kolejní
  street, nicknamed the **"Zeď nářků"** (Wailing Wall), departments paint joke drawings
  (csw:Pod_Palackého_vrchem).
- **Kounicovy koleje**: dorms built in 1922. During WWII they were a **prison and execution site**. Owned
  by the Veterinary University since 1999 (csw:Kounicovy_koleje). This is a dark place, so it does not
  suit a funny level.
- **Vinařská**: MU complex of 3 dorm blocks with a **menza** (canteen) and a gym, next to Výstaviště
  (https://www.skm.muni.cz/ubytovani/koleje-muni). MU runs 6 canteens and buffets, ordered through
  "WebKredit" (https://www.skm.muni.cz/stravovani/menzy-muni).
- **FIT VUT, Božetěchova 2**: the faculty sits inside the **Carthusian monastery founded in 1375**
  (Cella Trinitas). The emperor abolished it in 1782, it later became barracks, and VUT has held it since
  the 1960s. Hook: monks under a vow of silence → programmers (csw:Královopolský_klášter).
- **UKB Bohunice**: the biggest university construction project in Central Europe. 42 ha, 10,000 t of
  steel, **3,000 km of cables**, long connecting corridors (csw:Univerzitní_kampus_Bohunice). In the
  1920s **Kraví hora was planned** as the campus site (csw:Kraví_hora_(Brno)).
- **Mendelova univerzita**: founded 1919, focused on agriculture and forestry. Its horticulture faculty is
  in **Lednice**, the wheelwright's home town (csw:Mendelova_univerzita_v_Brně).
- **Majáles Brno**: a parade with **6 music floats** from nám. Svobody to Výstaviště. Students wear their
  university's colours, and a King and Queen are crowned (https://brno.majales.cz/pruvod/).
- **Lužánky**: founded 1786 as the first public park in the Czech lands (https://www.gotobrno.cz/misto/park-luzanky/).
  It has big lawns for picnics (https://vandrly.cz/mista/luzanky-brno). Slacklining and frisbee are
  **UNVERIFIED**.
- **Kraví hora**: a park, outdoor pool, observatory and baseball fields. Night line N89 runs nearby
  (csw:Kraví_hora_(Brno)). Wine at sunset is **UNVERIFIED** as a documented tradition; vineyards there
  are recorded from 1346.

## 5. Top 10 level concepts (ranked)

1. **Old Town Hall – Dragon & Wheel**: a boss crocodile that you beat by feeding it a quicklime sack. It
   gets thirsty, and a water power-up makes it burst. In a bonus section you roll Birck's wheel before the
   sunset timer runs out.
2. **Petrov – Noon at 11**: hold off the Swedish waves. Ringing the bell early ends the level, but only
   once the defence meter is full.
3. **Jakubák nightlife** (student): the stage is built on top of the ossuary. A "Na stojáka" mechanic means
   you can never sit down or stop moving, and the bum-man on the tower "moons" Petrov to stun enemies.
4. **Náměstí Svobody – the clock** (orloj): at 11:00 a marble rolls out into one of 4 holes; catch it to
   win. Reading the time on the clock is a puzzle.
5. **Noční rozjezd** (student): every N bus leaves the main station at the same moment. Pick the right one
   before they all go; the last one leaves within the hour.
6. **Zelný trh / Parnas**: climb the fountain's cliff while Cerberus and the rock bear guard it, with
   cabbage projectiles. Mozart's Reduta is the bonus stage.
7. **Old Town Hall portal – crooked pinnacle**: a "Pilgram didn't get paid" world where platforms bend
   unless you pay them in *love*.
8. **Palačák – Wall of Wailing** (student): spray "Ing." tags to unlock checkpoints. In the 5 canteens
   you queue for menza food.
9. **Vila Tugendhat**: the floor windows drop away under you, and the onyx wall shows hidden platforms
   only in sunset light.
10. **Prýgl + Ignis Brunensis**: ride the steamer while fireworks fire from the water; *jak švimhózny na
    priglu* is the gag line.

Other student options: the FIT monastery (a stealth level where you must stay silent), Majáles parade
floats as moving platforms, and the Bar that does not exist with its hidden entrance.

## 6. Follow-up (2026-10-18): Česká, FF MU, MZK, Kabinet múz

Same method (sourced; UNVERIFIED marked). `csw:<Title>` = `https://cs.wikipedia.org/wiki/<Title>`.

- **Česká / stop Česká ("Čára")** (csw:Česká_(Brno)): **7 tram lines** pass the stop and several
  trolleybus lines end there; the platforms wrap a whole block (Brandlova / Česká / Joštova /
  Moravské nám.). "**Na Čáře / pod hodinama**" is Brno's traditional meeting spot, named after a
  clock on a building corner where Česká widens into Joštova. Pedestrian zone (even bikes banned),
  a covered arcade along the Constitutional Court building, a "**pizza do ruky**" window since the
  early 1990s, Baťa department store, Hotel Avion. UNVERIFIED: which line numbers stop there.
- **Filozofická fakulta MU, Arna Nováka 1** (csw:Filozofická_fakulta_Masarykovy_univerzity):
  largest faculty in Czechia by students, founded 1919. **Building A was a boys' orphanage**
  (1871–72); early on the faculty shared it with the state railways directorate. Library = building F
  (2000–01, Grand Prix of the Architects' Society), 400 reader seats on 4 floors. Student café
  "**Krmítko**" in building J. UNVERIFIED: the nickname "Filda" (used anyway, it is the user's word).
- **Moravská zemská knihovna (MZK), Kounicova** (csw:Moravská_zemská_knihovna): **2nd largest
  library in Czechia**; first inventory entry (6 July 1808) is a book about seed loss in grain.
  Building opened 2001 (ONEX Praha). **Colour-coded floors**: 1st orange, 2nd–3rd red, 4th–5th blue,
  6th green, 7th yellow. "Tichá zóna v atriu", a chess corner, Milan Kundera Library (since 2023);
  books from the 4th floor up are reference only. UNVERIFIED: the nickname "MZKčko" (user's word).
- **Kabinet MÚZ, Sukova 49/4** (csw:Kabinet_múz; https://www.kabinetrecords.cz/kontakt/):
  alternative-music club, label Kabinet Records. Tenants since 1991: HaDivadlo (until 2003),
  Divadlo v 7 a půl (**evicted over rent debt**), JAMU drama students (**also left over the rent**,
  2009); reopened 2012; film series "**Kabinet Filmúz**" from 2016. Per the user: a place where
  queer people and intellectuals go out — portray it as celebrated, never as the joke.
